name: Bioclimatic Architecture
description: Design that responds to local climate — solar orientation, thermal mass, natural ventilation, shading — to reduce energy use. Rooted in vernacular building; formalized by Victor Olgyay and others.

name: Kinetic Architecture
description: Buildings and facades with moving parts that adapt to light, wind, or use — rotating, folding, and responsive structures. Blends architecture with engineering and computation.

name: Smart Building
description: Buildings instrumented with sensors and automation for energy, comfort, security, and space management. Includes building automation systems and IoT integration.

name: Wabi-Sabi
description: A Japanese aesthetic centered on imperfection, impermanence, and rustic simplicity — asymmetry, roughness, and the beauty of aging. Deeply influential in design, architecture, and craft.

name: Gesamtkunstwerk
description: The 'total work of art' — Wagner's ideal fusion of music, drama, poetry, and stagecraft into a unified whole. A concept that echoes through opera, film, and multimedia art.

name: Modular Synthesizer
description: A synthesizer composed of patchable modules — oscillators, filters, envelopes — connected by cables to create custom signal paths. The Moog and Eurorack formats; a cornerstone of electronic music.

name: Musique Concrète
description: Composition from recorded, manipulated real-world sounds on tape, pioneered by Pierre Schaeffer in 1940s Paris. The ancestor of sampling and sound collage.

name: Aleatoric Music
description: Music in which some element of composition or performance is left to chance, associated with John Cage and the 1950s avant-garde. Chance procedures replace fixed notation.

name: Microtonality
description: The use of intervals smaller than the Western semitone — quarter-tones, just intonation, and non-12-tone scales. Common in Arabic, Indian, and contemporary experimental music.

name: Generative Music
description: Music created by systems — algorithms, randomness, and rules — that unfold unpredictably, associated with Brian Eno. Overlaps with algorithmic and AI composition.

name: Field Recording
description: Recording environmental sound — nature, cities, machinery — outside the studio. Foundational to soundscape composition, documentary, and sound design.

name: Vaporwave
description: An internet-born microgenre of the 2010s that samples 80s-90s muzak, elevator music, and pop, slowed and filtered into nostalgic, ironic soundscapes.

name: City Pop
description: Japanese urban pop of the late 1970s-80s blending funk, jazz-fusion, and yacht rock. Revived globally through YouTube algorithms and lo-fi nostalgia.

name: Grime
description: A UK electronic genre born in early-2000s London, fusing fast 140-BPM beats with MCing and pirate-radio culture. Distinct from hip-hop; led by Wiley and Dizzee Rascal.

name: Qawwali
description: Sufi devotional music of South Asia — passionate vocal performances accompanied by harmonium and tabla, built on poetry of divine love. Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan brought it global renown.

name: Kinetic Art
description: Art that incorporates actual or apparent motion — motors, wind, light — associated with Alexander Calder's mobiles and the 1960s. Movement is the medium.

name: ASCII Art
description: Images constructed from text characters on early terminals and typewriters. A low-tech precursor to pixel art and a staple of early computer culture.

name: AI Art
description: Artworks generated or co-created with machine-learning models — GANs, diffusion models, and text-to-image systems. Raises deep questions of authorship, copyright, and creativity.

name: Soulslike
description: Action RPGs defined by punishing difficulty, deliberate combat, and environmental storytelling, following FromSoftware's Demon's Souls and Dark Souls. A named subgenre with a devoted community.

name: Rhythm Game
description: Games where players act in time with music — Dance Dance Revolution, Guitar Hero, osu!. Precision timing is the core mechanic.

name: Idle / Clicker Game
description: Games that progress with minimal input, using timers, exponential numbers, and incremental upgrades — Cookie Clicker, AdVenture Capitalist. A study in compulsion loops.

name: Kanban
description: A visual scheduling system from Toyota using cards and boards to limit work-in-progress and pull work through a process. Core to lean and agile software.

name: Kaizen
description: The Japanese practice of continuous, incremental improvement involving all employees. A pillar of Toyota's production system and lean manufacturing.

name: OKR (Objectives & Key Results)
description: A goal-setting framework pairing qualitative objectives with measurable key results, popularized by Intel and Google. Aligns teams and tracks ambition.

name: ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance)
description: The framework for evaluating corporate sustainability — environmental impact, social responsibility, and governance. Now central to investment and disclosure.

name: Gig Economy
description: Labor markets structured around short-term, platform-mediated freelance work — ride-hailing, delivery, freelance marketplaces. Raises questions of worker classification and precarity.

name: Sharing Economy
description: Peer-to-peer access to underused assets — homes, cars, tools — mediated by platforms like Airbnb and Uber. Blurs ownership and consumption.

name: Decolonial Thought
description: Critique of colonial power in knowledge, institutions, and culture, seeking epistemic and material decolonization. Associated with Fanon, Mignolo, and Indigenous scholarship.

name: CUDA
description: NVIDIA's parallel-computing platform and programming model for general-purpose GPU computing. The foundation of modern deep learning and scientific computing.

name: Protein Structure Prediction
description: Computational prediction of protein 3D structure from amino-acid sequence. Transformed by deep-learning systems like AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold.
